name: generic_axes_diagram
description: Any single-panel curve diagram that is not a supply/demand market: production functions, cost/utility curves, dose-response, growth/decay, diminishing returns. Choose this scene for ANY single-curve or multi-curve (up to 4) plot against generic axes. Curves are qualitative shapes (linear_up/linear_down/convex_up/concave_down/s_curve/u_shape/bell) or an exact expression y=f(x); points, vertical/horizontal reference lines, and a shaded region between two curves (or under one) are all optional. All geometry is computed for you.

id.description: Custom element id for this curve; default "curve_<i>".

expression.description: y = f(x) over x ∈ [0, 100], e.g. "80*(1 - exp(-0.05*x))". Wins over `shape` when both are set.

shape.description: A canned qualitative shape, used when `expression` is not set. Default "linear_up".

curves.description: 1–4 curves, each y = f(x) over x ∈ [0, 100].

shade.description: Shade a region under one curve or between two curves, over [x_from, x_to]. Set exactly one of `between`/`under`.

between.description: Indices into `curves` of the two curves to shade between.

under.description: Index into `curves` of the curve to shade under, down to y = 0.

element_ids.curve_<i>: curve i (or its own `id`, when set)
element_ids.label_<curve id>: that curve's label, when it has one
element_ids.title: figure title, when set

examples.request: Draw a production function with diminishing returns.
Draw a dose-response curve and mark the half-maximal dose.
